assumptions: Attackers (e.g., internal users or tools) can send HTTP requests to the /api/snippets/download endpoint and control the path query parameter arbitrarily; they are not limited to values previously returned by the create_snippet endpoint.
The service runs with filesystem permissions that allow it to read files above settings.storage_root, such as application source or config under /home/user/projects.

No additional middleware, reverse proxy, or framework layer performs path canonicalization or enforces that only files under settings.storage_root can be served before the request reaches this handler.
vulnerability_candidate.description: Directory traversal in the /api/snippets/download endpoint allows reading arbitrary files outside the configured storage_root. The handler takes the path query parameter directly from the request, passes it to storage.get_snippet_file, which only strips leading slashes and then joins it with settings.storage_root. Because there is no normalization or check to keep the result within storage_root, an attacker can supply values containing .. segments (for example, ../../projects/omnicore/config/settings.yml) so that the resulting filesystem path points to files above the snippet directory. If those files exist and are readable by the service account, Flask's send_file will return their contents, exposing application configuration or other sensitive data under /home/user.

    """

    # Normalise a leading slash if clients accidentally include one.

    return os.path.join(settings.storage_root, rel_path)
